Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Body, health & movement

tall adjective

also taller, how tall, grow taller, a tall tree, a head taller than, he is tall, be a head taller than

classical

Ov. M. 13.790: longā prōcērior alnō (Lewis & Short)
Suet. Vesp. 23: homō prōcērae statūrae (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 158

prōcērus, prōcēra, prōcērum

tall, long

Tall and slender: of people, necks and trees (Cicero’s prōcērissimae populī, Leg. 1.15). To ask how tall someone is, Latin asks about statūra, height: quā statūrā (Cic. Phil. 2.41, below).

Other words

  • altus, alta, altum — high, tall

    also used · classical · Ov. M. 3.181: altior illīs ipsa dea est (Lewis & Short); Traupman 158

    High, of whatever rises, seen from below: walls, trees, mountains; less often of people. It also means deep (seen from above), and of the mind lofty (Lewis & Short; see height).

  • excelsus, excelsa, excelsum — lofty, towering

    also used · classical · Publ. Syr. E 16: Excelsīs multō facilius cāsus nocet.

    High up, towering, and so eminent, noble (animus excelsus, Cic.; Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • velim mihi dīcās, L. Turselius quā faciē fuerit, quā statūrā

    I should like you to tell me what Lucius Turselius looked like and how tall he wasCic. Phil. 2.41 (Lewis & Short)

  • corporaque eōrum inprōcēra fierī minusque adolēscere

    and their bodies stay short and grow up lessGell. 4.19.1

  • Redīstī prōcērior. — At equidem māllem prūdentior, aut doctior.

    You’ve come back taller! — I’d rather have come back wiser, or more learned.Erasm. Coll., Fōrm., Percontandī dē valētūdine, I 12

  • tōtō vertice esse suprā (+ acc.)

    to be a head taller thanTraupman 390

  • Statūrā prōcērā est.

    He is tall.Traupman 390

  • tōtō vertice suprā est

    he is taller by a whole headVerg. A. 7.784 (Lewis & Short s.v. vertex); Traupman 326

See also short, height, big, tower.
